response: {"title":"Normalize-versus-validate pair","intervention":"At each edited parsing or coercion boundary, test one raw input and its normalized counterpart and assert whether validation must occur before or after normalization, including the exact return or exception class and message for both.","claim":"Compared with no appended instruction, this paired normalization check will improve held-out boundary and invalid-input pass_rate on matched Python tasks within the same deadline, with wall_time and turns tracked.","mechanism":"Paired raw and canonical values reveal ordering bugs where trimming, case-folding, numeric coercion, or decoding accidentally converts an invalid input into a valid one or changes the observable error.","assumptions":["Affected modules contain parsing, coercion, or normalization boundaries.","Repository evidence specifies the intended order of normalization and validation.","Representative raw/canonical pairs can be constructed cheaply."],"risks":["The intended normalization policy may be undocumented.","One pair may not cover interactions among multiple normalization steps.","Strict pre-normalization rejection can harm deliberately permissive APIs.","Exact errors may differ legitimately across parser backends."],"test_plan":{"experiment":"Randomly assign matched multi-module Python repairs to this appended instruction or no appended instruction under identical model, tools, and deadline; score hidden raw/canonical pairs plus boundary, invalid-input, exception-class, and exact-message cases.","metrics":["pass_rate","wall_time","turns"],"success_condition":"The intervention arm has higher hidden pass_rate on normalization-order and overall edge semantics, completes within the deadline, and does not materially increase median turns."},"single_shot_ordinal":12}
